question: What was the original official name of the English East India Company when it was formed in London?
options: The Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies
The United Company of Merchants of England Trading to the East Indies
The British East India Mercantile Association
The London and Canton Royal Trading Company
explanation: The original name of the company as chartered in 1600 was 'The Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies'. It is commonly abbreviated as the English East India Company.

question: Who was appointed as the first Governor of the English East India Company?
explanation: Sir Thomas Smythe, a prominent London merchant and governor of the Levant Company, was designated as the first Governor of the newly formed East India Company by the Charter of 1600.
